chain.label: FAA does not require CO detectors or enhanced exhaust inspections
chain.trigger: the FAA does not require CO detectors on enclosed-cabin general aviation aircraft with reciprocating engines

chain.label: Exhaust system failures missed during inspections; no pressure check performed
chain.trigger: maintenance personnel have likely missed exhaust system failures during inspections

caused_by.evidence: the exhaust system had not been pressure checked (to identify holes in the muffler) as recommended in the FAA's enhanced inspection standards, but such an inspection was not required

chain.label: Corroded muffler with holes and wall thickness loss
chain.trigger: Examination of the two muffler assemblies revealed holes and wall thickness loss around the right muffler body

caused_by.evidence: one of the airplane's two mufflers, which was replaced 742.9 flight hours before the accident flight, had corroded and that the muffler's walls were thin and had pin holes

chain.label: Exhaust system leak introduced CO into the enclosed cabin
chain.trigger: a defect, leak, or failure in the aircraft's exhaust pipes, muffler, or heat transfer system can introduce CO into the enclosed cabin

caused_by.evidence: holes and wall thickness loss around the right muffler body, which likely introduced CO into the cabin

chain.label: No CO detector installed, or only a passive spot detector with no active alert
chain.trigger: The airplane's CO detector was a type known as a 'spot' detector, a passive CO alerting device that turns dark in the presence of CO; it does not include an active aural or visual alert

caused_by.evidence: A lack of required minimum standards for CO detectors can result in ineffective alerting if detectors do not meet those standards

chain.label: Pilot not alerted to and did not recognize CO exposure in time
chain.trigger: the pilot was not alerted to CO entering the cabin in enough time to counteract the effects of CO poisoning

caused_by.evidence: CO is a colorless, odorless, and tasteless gas... can go unnoticed by pilots or passengers
If the device is not built to an aviation-appropriate minimum performance standard, it may not appropriately alert the pilot in a timely manner to avoid a crash

chain.label: CO poisoning impaired judgment and incapacitated the pilot
chain.trigger: The NTSB determined the probable cause of the accident was pilot incapacitation due to CO poisoning

caused_by.evidence: Toxicology testing of the pilot's blood indicated an impairing level of CO
continued exposure can lead to impaired judgment and decreased ability to control the aircraft

chain.label: Loss of aircraft control due to degraded flying ability
chain.trigger: the airplane broke up in flight after the pilot's loss of control due to CO poisoning

caused_by.evidence: the pilot's flying abilities had degraded due to CO poisoning

chain.trigger: the airplane broke up in flight after the pilot's loss of control
